bullets.text: ML is a subfield of AI, learning from data without explicit programming.
Systems identify patterns and make decisions with minimal human intervention.
Widely applied in image recognition, NLP, predictive analytics, and autonomous systems.
Growth driven by large datasets, computational power, and advanced algorithms.
Supervised Learning: Models trained on labeled data for prediction (e.g., regression, classification).
Unsupervised Learning: Algorithms identify hidden patterns in unlabeled data (e.g., clustering, dimensionality reduction).
Reinforcement Learning: Agent learns to maximize cumulative rewards through environmental interaction.
Model Training: Algorithms learn from data, adjusting parameters to minimize prediction errors.
Features and Labels: Input variables (features) used for prediction vs. target outputs (labels).
Training and Testing Sets: Data split for model learning and performance evaluation on unseen data.
Overfitting and Underfitting: Model issues where it learns training data too well (including noise) or is too simple.
Linear & Logistic Regression: Models relationships for continuous outcomes and predicts probabilities for classification.
Decision Trees & Random Forest: Non-linear models that split data, with Random Forest being an ensemble for improved accuracy.
Support Vector Machines (SVM): Finds optimal hyperplanes to separate different classes.
Neural Networks: Brain-inspired models capable of learning complex patterns, widely used in deep learning.
Healthcare: Disease diagnosis, drug discovery, and personalized treatment.
Finance: Fraud detection, credit scoring, and algorithmic trading.
Marketing: Customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, and targeted advertising.
Autonomous Vehicles: Powers navigation, decision-making, and perception.
Natural Language Processing (NLP): Core technology for language translation, sentiment analysis, and text summarization.
Training and Testing: Performance evaluated using metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, MSE, or R-squared.
Cross-Validation: Ensures models generalize well to unseen data by splitting datasets into multiple subsets.
Hyperparameter Tuning: Optimizing pre-set model values using methods like grid search or random search for optimal performance.
Data Quality and Quantity: Requires large, accurate datasets for effective training.
Interpretability: Many complex models, especially deep learning, are difficult to understand.
Bias in Data: Models can inherit and perpetuate biases present in the training data.
Overfitting and Underfitting: Common issues impacting a model's ability to generalize to new data.
Rapid evolution with advances in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and explainable AI (XAI).
Increased integration into healthcare, education, entertainment, and transportation.
Crucial emphasis on ethical and responsible AI practices.
